samples.summary: setTheme() now repaints the whole preview, discarding DOM-only preview state its existing consumers rely on (expanded <details>, preview scroll position)
samples.evidence: The consumer that trips this is packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:112 — a light/dark toggle calls `editorRef.current.setTheme(...)`, which now runs `renderPreview()` (editor.ts:443) → `NotePreview.render()` → `this.el.innerHTML = md.render(...)` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:198). That wipes DOM-only state the shipped collapsible-sections feature (issue #542, packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts) depends on: any `<details>` the reader manually expanded collapses back to its source-derived `open` state, and the preview scroll position resets to the top. Previously a theme toggle only reconfigured the CodeMirror theme compartment and left the preview DOM untouched; in `view` (reading) mode nothing else triggers a repaint, so this is newly reachable for a reader who is not typing. Fix belongs on the new code (repaint only blocks that actually contain a `.note-mermaid` placeholder, or preserve scrollTop/open state across the theme repaint).

samples.summary: NoteEditorAPI.dispose() does not cancel an in-flight mermaid pass, so work continues (and touches document.body) after the React consumer unmounts
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:103 calls `editor.dispose()` on unmount; packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:481-488 tears down listeners and destroys the CodeMirror view but never signals the preview. A pass queued on the module-global `passChain` (mermaid.ts:413/407) keeps running after that: `passSeq` is only bumped by a new `render()`, so `superseded()` is false, and `root.contains(el)` is true for a *detached* preview subtree (the root still contains its own children). The pass therefore still awaits `import('mermaid')`, runs a full layout, appends and removes mermaid's `d<id>` host div on the live `document.body` (mermaid.ts:481), and paints into an orphaned tree — after the notes route has been navigated away from, and twice under React StrictMode's double mount. No data loss, but it is work and a chunk download the disposed consumer explicitly asked to stop. A `dispose()` hook on NotePreview (or bumping the root's generation from dispose) would close it.

samples.summary: mermaid drags Node-only transitive deps (@iconify/utils → @antfu/install-pkg → tinyexec / import-meta-resolve) into the frontend browser bundle graph; only two diagram types were verified in a browser
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:229 aliases `@wafflebase/notes` to source, so `import('mermaid')` (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:139) is bundled by the frontend build. The lockfile adds `@iconify/utils@3.1.4` → `@antfu/install-pkg@1.1.0` → `tinyexec` / `import-meta-resolve` (pnpm-lock.yaml, new `@antfu/install-pkg` entry), which reach `node:child_process`/`node:fs`. Vite externalizes node builtins for browser targets with a throwing stub rather than failing the build, so this surfaces only at runtime, and only on the mermaid diagram types that touch the icon loader (architecture/icon diagrams). docs/tasks/active/20260803-notes-mermaid-preview-todo.md:97-99 declares this settled, but the browser check it cites covered only `flowchart` and `sequenceDiagram` (line 90), which do not exercise the icon path. Degradation would be a per-diagram error label, not a crash. Confirming needs a browser render of an `architecture-beta` fence.

samples.summary: Engine/cache/theme state is module-global rather than per-preview, so any second NotePreview instance shares the queue and the last-initialized palette
samples.evidence: `renderCache` (mermaid.ts:112), `loaded` (133), `initializedTheme` (134), `purifier` (155) and `passChain` (413) are module singletons, while `NotePreview` is instantiated per editor mount (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:177). Two live previews — React StrictMode's double mount at packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:85-108, or any future second notes surface — serialize behind one chain and re-`initialize()` mermaid for each other's theme; the only way to reset is the test-only `resetMermaidStateForTests()` (mermaid.ts:511), which no production path calls. Today both instances share the app theme so the visible effect is bounded to queueing delay, but the invariant "one engine config per preview" is not enforced anywhere.

samples.summary: Design doc records a different measured notes-view growth than harness.config.json from the same change
samples.evidence: docs/design/notes/notes.md:343 says `notes-view-*.js` grew 2.25 kB, while the harness reason added in this change states "notes-view-*.js measured 1298.92 kB → 1302.82 kB (+3.90 kB)" (harness.config.json, maxChunkCountReason). The todo notes a re-measure against the rebased tree (docs/tasks/active/20260803-notes-mermaid-preview-todo.md:80) that updated the harness figure but not the design doc, so the nested design doc now documents a stale number — and nested design docs are not covered by any CI check.

samples.summary: A version-pin test makes any routine mermaid patch/minor upgrade fail the notes suite, and depends on mermaid exposing ./package.json through its exports map
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:258-260 requires `mermaid/package.json` and asserts its version equals `MERMAID_CARRIER_PATTERNS_VERSION` (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:200). Two out-of-diff consequences: (1) the repo has a recurring dependency-bump workflow (docs/tasks/archive/2026/08/20260806-dependabot-alerts-todo.md and several earlier ones), and every mermaid bump under `^11.16.0` will now red the `@wafflebase/notes` suite until someone re-diffs upstream regexes — intended per the comment, but it is a new hard gate on an automated pipeline nobody has been told about; (2) `require('mermaid/package.json')` only resolves if mermaid's `exports` map exposes that subpath, which I could not verify here (dependencies are not installed in this checkout).
